narrative.title: The Knockout Bracket Blueprint
narrative.scenario: A tournament organizer is drafting a single-elimination bracket on a whiteboard. The first round is a single title-holder at the top, and every subsequent round can field at most twice as many contenders as the round before it, because each slot in a round spawns at most two slots in the next. The organizer wants a one-line formula so the venue can be sized for any round number without redrawing the whole board.
narrative.inputFormat: A single integer n — the 1-indexed level of the binary tree.
narrative.outputFormat: Return one integer: the maximum number of nodes that can exist on level n.
constraints: The answer always fits in a 32-bit signed integer for the given range

testCases.explanation: Level 1 holds only the root, so the cap is 1.
Doubling each round: level 2 holds 2, level 3 holds 2^(3-1) = 4.

hintLevels: Level 1: Picture each level of the tree as a round of a tournament — every node can parent at most two children on the next level.
Level 2: Track the headcount level by level: 1, 2, 4, 8 — each entry is double the previous one.
Level 3: Close the pattern into a closed form: the cap for level n is 2^(n-1), computed in a single exponentiation with no loops needed.
